evidence.note: Created a TodoWrite plan and de-risked foundations first: checked Rust toolchain, tree-sitter availability, crates.io access before committing to an approach.

Built layers in explicit dependency order — Cargo.toml, main.rs (stdio/protocol plumbing), analyzer.rs (AST/symbol model), handlers.rs (method handlers) — then a baseline build and run_tests, establishing each layer minimally works before proceeding.
Spiked the riskiest foundation early: built a throwaway binary and 'AST printer' to explore tree-sitter output before relying on it for parsing/analysis.

Tackled methods one at a time (foldingRange, hover, callHierarchy, references, documentHighlight, codeLens, documentSymbol, typeDefinition, selectionRange), each as diagnose→edit→run_tests with a concrete pass-count done-check.

Recurring TodoWrite milestone updates plus periodic 'Total'/'Run actual scoring' checks show milestone tracking sustained across the full horizon, with later methods reusing the validated symbol model.

reasoning: The agent laid out an explicit milestone hierarchy — protocol layer, then parser/AST, then symbol model, then a method-by-method handler sequence — with each layer having a concrete completion check (build passes, handshake responds, per-method pass counts via run_tests), and later methods built on the validated analyzer, matching the level-8 anchor. It even de-risked the parser foundation with an early tree-sitter spike and batched shared-machinery methods. It falls short of 10 because the method ordering reads as opportunistic (start with cheap structural folding, then iterate) rather than a documented prioritization explicitly reasoned by leverage and cost-to-pass.
